deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is setting up a theory of 'equisingular' decompositions (stratifications) of spaces as a foundation for 'topologie modérée'. On the previous page he defined an equisingular partition of X into 'leaves' F_i. Conditions: each F_i is locally closed (closure and boundary bF_i = cl(F_i) - F_i are closed); each closure is a union of leaves (the frontier condition); and the diagram of X with the leaf-closures and inclusions is equisingular along every leaf. Incidence (inclusion of closures) orders the set of leaves.

NB on this page: two different equisingular filtrations of X can induce the same partition into leaves. The partition, i.e. the poset of strata, is the essential datum, not the filtration. In the piecewise (PL, semi-algebraic, subanalytic) context, where dimension and codimension are available, there are at least four canonical filtrations attached to a given equisingular partition, distinct in general:
1) the skeleton filtration X_i = union of leaves of dimension <= i;
2) the 'depth from below' filtration: X_0 = union of minimal leaves for the incidence order, and X_i = X_{i-1} together with the leaves minimal among those not contained in X_{i-1};
3) and 4) the dual versions (by codimension, or starting from the maximal leaves), which give decreasing filtrations.
Conclusion: from now on he works with spaces equipped with equisingular partitions, i.e. stratified spaces, rather than filtered spaces.

A proposition is begun and struck out: that closed unions of leaves inherit an equisingular partition.

Then diagrams: let (X_i)_{i in I} be a diagram of spaces, each with a partition. The system of partitions is admissible if (a) each partition is admissible (locally closed leaves plus the frontier condition), and (b) every transition map X_i -> X_j sends each leaf of X_i into a single, uniquely determined leaf of X_j.

On the next page this yields a diagram of posets of strata P_i -> P_j and a diagram of maps between closed leaves. Equisingularity of the system is defined, then 'privileged' systems (leaf closures are manifolds). Conjecture 1 follows: in the PL/algebraic/analytic piecewise context, every space has a privileged partition, and there is a coarsest one, the 'canonical' one.
errors: Filtration 2 as written ('X_i = réunion des feuilles minimales parmi celles qui sont not in X_{i-1}') must implicitly include X_{i-1} to give an increasing filtration by closed sets. As literally written, X_i consists only of the newly minimal leaves. This is a minor slip.

Claims about 'four canonical filtrations, distinct in general' are not proved. The duals of 1) and 2) give decreasing filtrations by open (not closed) unions of leaves, which is consistent with the frontier condition but not stated.

ideas.what: The stratification (partition into leaves with its incidence poset) is the primary datum; filtrations are only presentations of it
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified spaces (X -> P), as opposed to filtered spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in Thom–Mather / Goresky–MacPherson; poset-indexed formalism systematized by Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A, ~2009–2017), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tame topology and stratified structures only in general terms

ideas.what: Four canonical filtrations attached to a stratification: by dimension, by depth from minimal strata, and their duals
ideas.modern_name: Skeleta / dimension filtration; depth (height) filtration of the stratum poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Thom, Mather, Goresky–MacPherson; depth in Siebenmann's and Mather's work)

ideas.what: Admissible system of partitions on a diagram of spaces: transition maps send strata into strata, inducing a diagram of posets of strata
ideas.modern_name: Diagrams of stratified spaces / stratified maps compatible with maps of stratifying posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (stratified maps, 1969); modern functorial treatment in Lurie and Haine

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly abandons filtered spaces in favour of spaces with stratifications whose poset of strata is the invariant. He makes this functorial in diagrams (maps of strata posets P_i -> P_j). This anticipates the modern 'stratified space over a poset' formalism by decades, but it is a natural viewpoint and largely standard.
missed.quote: C'est la partition en feuilles qui est la plus importante, non la filtration.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents Grothendieck's 1974 preference for poset-stratified language, relevant to the genealogy of exit-path / stratified homotopy theory. It is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: Definitional, foundational material on stratifications. It is conceptually consonant with later poset-stratified formalisms, but contains no result absent from the literature. The interesting conjecture (a coarsest canonical privileged stratification) is on the next page.
transcription_corrections: '(évidemment unique déterminée)' should read '(évidemment uniquement déterminée)'.
Struck proposition reads roughly: 'Prop. Si la partition donnée de X est équisingulière, alors [pour toute partie fermée] de X qui est réunion de feuilles, la partition induite est équisingulière'.
Line '3° et 4° définitions "duales" de 1° et 2°, donnant des filtrations décroissantes': 'décroissantes' is underlined in the original.
